title: Databricks
summary: Problems whose patterns are commonly reported in Databricks coding interviews, from Easy to Hard. Approximate and hand curated, not an official or verified question list.
lesson:
About this list
- Each problem practices a pattern that candidates commonly describe from Databricks coding interviews: versioned and timestamped storage (snapshots, time-series counters), k-way merging and external-sort patterns, interval coverage and querying, caches, sliding-window aggregations, and task scheduling.
- Problems are grouped Easy, Medium, and Hard so you can warm up on binary search and merging before practicing high-throughput data structures and range queries.
- The selection is approximate. Interview rounds vary by team and level, so treat this track as data-systems pattern practice rather than a prediction of what you will be asked.

What to expect
- Candidates often report data-intensive and systems-flavored algorithm questions: rolling hit counters, versioned snapshots, merging sorted streams, interval queries, and O(1) or O(log n) stateful structures.
- Interviewers commonly probe memory footprint, amortized vs. worst-case latency, and how your design handles sparse keys, out-of-order timestamps, or large streams.
- Clean APIs and tight asymptotic complexity matter equally; brute-force full-array copies or linear scans are typically rejected in follow-ups.

How to prepare
- Practice combining hash maps with ordered structures (sorted arrays + binary search, heaps, or doubly linked lists) to hit O(1) or O(log n) per operation.
- Pay close attention to sparse memory representations and boundary conditions on time windows and half-open vs. closed intervals.
- After passing, practice explaining how you would partition or shard the structure across nodes.
